title: The Manifest Victory (Fath Mubin)
subtitle: Surah Al-Fath and the Peaceful Expansion of Islam
summary: The revelation of Surah Al-Fath on the road back from Hudaybiyyah, Umar's realization of true victory, the rapid peaceful expansion of Islam during the ten-year truce, Abu Basir's coastal stronghold nullifying the extradition clause, and the conversion of military titans Khalid ibn al-Walid and Amr ibn al-Aas.

sections.text: The Revelation on the Road: Surah Al-Fath

On the return march from Hudaybiyyah, while the companions were still grappling with the apparent sting of turning back without performing Umrah, divine revelation descended upon the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ at a waystation near Kara' al-Ghamim. The Prophet called for Umar ibn al-Khattab and proclaimed with radiant joy: 'Tonight, a surah has been revealed to me that is dearer to me than the entire world and everything within it!' He then recited the opening of Surah Al-Fath:

إِنَّا فَتَحْنَا لَكَ فَتْحًا مُّبِينًا ۝ لِّيَغْفِرَ لَكَ اللَّهُ مَا تَقَدَّمَ مِن ذَنبِكَ وَمَا تَأَخَّرَ وَيُتِمَّ نِعْمَتَهُ عَلَيْكَ وَيَهْدِيَكَ صِرَاطًا مُّسْتَقِيمًا
'Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest—that Allah may forgive you what preceded of your sin and what will follow and complete His favor upon you and guide you to a straight path.' (Surah Al-Fath 48:1–2)

Umar looked at the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in astonishment, asking: 'Is this truly a victory, O Messenger of Allah?' The Prophet replied with absolute conviction: 'Yes, by Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, it is indeed a victory!'

History soon validated the profound divine truth of that declaration. In the previous nineteen years, the Muslims and the pagan tribes had lived in constant warfare and visceral fear. The ten-year armistice agreed at Hudaybiyyah dismantled the psychological barriers dividing Arabia. With peace established, people met, traveled freely, engaged in intellectual and spiritual dialogues, and heard the Qur'an without the cloud of wartime hostility. Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri, the celebrated early historian, recorded that in the two years between the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah and the Conquest of Makkah, more people entered Islam than in all the preceding years of the mission combined.
Abu Basir & The Unraveling Extradition Clause

The controversial extradition clause—requiring Muslims escaping Makkah to be returned—unraveled through unexpected divine wisdom. A young Makkan convert named Abu Basir Utbah ibn Usayd escaped to Madinah. Quraysh dispatched two emissaries with a formal letter demanding his return. True to his word, the Prophet ﷺ handed Abu Basir over to them. On the journey back to Makkah, Abu Basir cleverly disarmed one of his guards at Dhu al-Hulayfah, killing him in combat while the other fled in terror back to Madinah.

Recognizing that staying in Madinah would compromise the Prophet's treaty obligations, Abu Basir slipped away to the Red Sea coastal route at Al-Is. He was soon joined by Abu Jandal and seventy other oppressed Muslim youths who had broken out of Makkan prisons. This independent band established a base that severed Quraysh's northern trade caravans to Syria, bringing Makkan commerce to a standstill. Desperate, Quraysh sent envoys to the Prophet pleading with him, by the ties of kinship, to invite Abu Basir and his companions into Madinah and officially cancel the extradition clause! Thus, the single clause that had broken the companions' hearts was discarded at Quraysh's own urgent petition.
The Conversion of Khalid and Amr

The moral prestige of Hudaybiyyah captivated the greatest military minds of Arabia. Khalid ibn al-Walid, the undefeated cavalry genius who had turned the tide at Uhud, realized that the truth of Islam was irresistible. Simultaneously, Amr ibn al-Aas, the sharpest political mind of Quraysh, arrived at the same conviction. The two legendary champions met on the desert highway riding toward Madinah to submit to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When they entered the Prophet's Mosque, the Prophet beamed with radiant happiness, exclaiming to his companions: 'Makkah has cast down to you the dearest pieces of its liver!'

references.title: The Holy Quran
references.author: Surah Al-Fath (48:1–5)
references.notes: Divine confirmation designating the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah as a 'Manifest Victory' (Fathan Mubina).

references.title: Sahih al-Bukhari
references.author: Imam Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Bukhari (d. 256 AH)
references.source: Kitab al-Maghazi, Bab Ghazwat al-Hudaybiyyah, Hadith 4177–4182
references.notes: The revelation of Surah al-Fath on the return from Hudaybiyyah is Muslim 1786, cited in the next reference, not this Bukhari span. Abu Basir at al-Is is classical sirah. The span 4177–4182 was not re-opened number by number and is not asserted as the source of that episode.

references.title: Sahih Muslim
references.author: Imam Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj (d. 261 AH)
references.notes: Anas: on the return from Hudaybiyyah, 'Indeed, We have given you a clear victory' was revealed, and the Prophet said a verse had come down that was dearer to him than the world. This Hadith does not report the acceptance of Islam by Khalid ibn al-Walid or Amr ibn al-As. Those conversions remain the classical sirah.
